name: Behind-the-meter power for compute
title: Behind-the-meter power for data centers: ripe, or not yet?
question: Is behind-the-meter power for data centers ripe?
answer: Grid interconnection queues stretch for years while compute demand surges, and stationary storage prices fell sharply in 2025, to about $70/kWh by BloombergNEF's survey as cited in 2026 research. Siting generation and storage at the data center sidesteps the queue. The open check: the companies said to have died trying this in the 2010s, at $400+/kWh storage, are asserted but not yet named.
verdict_reason: The crossing looks real; the graveyard is asserted at cohort level and must be enumerated before a ripe call.

constraint.name: Storage cost and grid access
constraint.detail: On-site generation needs cheap storage to be firm, and it is only worth the trouble when grid connection is slow or scarce.

crossing.text: Storage price survey: about $70/kWh, down about 45% in a year (BloombergNEF, as cited in 2026 research).

graveyard_note: Asserted, not enumerated: the 2026-08-01 research names 'the 2010s microgrid cohort' and demand-response firms. Until named, funded companies that died on storage cost are sourced, this cannot be called ripe.

evidence.text: Stationary storage price about $70/kWh, down about 45% year on year (BloombergNEF survey, as cited in the 2026-08-01 research; not independently checked).
evidence.unlinked: BloombergNEF data is not redistributable; figure as cited in research notes
